The Battle of Ðocaj and Jasić (also spelled Đocaj and Jasić) was a clash that took place in July 1998 during the Kosovo War, near the villages of Ðocaj and Jasić in western Kosovo, close to the Kosovo–Albania border.
Background
During the summer of 1998, western Kosovo, particularly the areas near the Kosovo–Albania border, was the scene of repeated clashes between the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) and forces of the Yugoslav Army (VJ). Control of villages in this region was strategically important for supply and movement.
Battle
KLA units engaged Yugoslav Army forces in Ðocaj and Jasić. After the fighting, KLA forces captured the villages. Several Yugoslav Army officers were killed during the battle, including Goran Ostojić, Dragan Dušanić, and Srđan Stančetić.
Agim Ramadani participated in the operations as a KLA commander but survived; he was later killed in April 1999 during the Battle of Košare.
Aftermath
The capture of Ðocaj and Jasić strengthened KLA territorial presence in western Kosovo and contributed to further operations along the Kosovo–Albania border.
